# Motion patterns

<!-- Generated by docs/build_motion_patterns.mjs from skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/. Edit the pattern pages, then run the script. -->

brief2motion carries 27 motion pattern recipes: the scroll animations, hover effects, page transitions and 3D moments that briefs ask for most. Each recipe says when to use the pattern and when not, which stack builds it, a performance and accessibility budget, what the page does for a visitor who has reduced motion switched on, and how the checks verify it. The router (`scripts/route.mjs`) lists the patterns whose words appear in a brief, and the agent starts from the recipe's sketch.

The sketches are starting points, not tested pages: their JavaScript parses and the kit files they import exist (`tests/patterns.test.mjs`). The tested pages are the [examples](../examples/). Every pattern follows the same frame: content is in the HTML and readable without JavaScript, motion is created only when the visitor has not asked for reduced motion, and the page reports its motion state so the checker can test both branches. The timing and easing rules all of them share are in [motion-doctrine.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/motion-doctrine.md).

## The patterns

### Hero load sequence

The first screen sets itself in a short, ordered sequence: headline first, then the supporting line, the action and the product picture. Most pages need this one planned entrance and little else.

- **Use when:** the brief says the hero should "animate in", "set itself", "feel alive on load", or a launch page needs a first impression.
- **Not when:** the page must be readable at once (a pricing or docs page), or the sequence would delay the main action by more than about a second. Never put the hero behind a loader.
- **Reduced motion:** No movement. The finished hero is on screen, and `signal('reduced')` says so. A fade of under 0.2 s is allowed but not needed.
- **Recipe:** [hero-load-sequence.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/hero-load-sequence.md)

### Text line reveal

A headline rises line by line from behind an invisible edge, so each line appears to be set into place.

- **Use when:** a type-led page, a headline that carries the brief, a section title that should feel crafted.
- **Not when:** body text, long paragraphs, or more than two reveals on one page (it stops being special). Not for text that must be readable while it moves.
- **Reduced motion:** `gsap.matchMedia()` creates the motion only inside the no-preference branch. In the reduced branch nothing is created, so the heading is the plain, finished text.
- **Recipe:** [text-line-reveal.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/text-line-reveal.md)

### Words that read themselves

A paragraph starts dim and each word lights up as it crosses the screen, so the page paces the reading.

- **Use when:** a manifesto, a mission paragraph or a single key statement that should be read slowly, once.
- **Not when:** more than one such paragraph per page, long text, or any text the reader needs at once. Dim words must still pass contrast (see Budget).
- **Reduced motion:** `--w` is never set, so every word is at full opacity. Nothing scrolls differently.
- **Recipe:** [word-by-word-read.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/word-by-word-read.md)

### Mask reveal

A picture or panel is uncovered by a moving edge (a wipe), while the picture inside settles from slightly larger.

- **Use when:** hero or gallery images, project covers, a section that needs a deliberate "uncover" beat.
- **Not when:** every image on the page, or images that carry information the reader needs at once (a chart, a screenshot of the product being explained).
- **Reduced motion:** No animation is created; the full image is on screen.
- **Recipe:** [mask-reveal.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/mask-reveal.md)

### Number counter

A figure counts up to its real value when it scrolls into view.

- **Use when:** one to four headline figures (customers served, hours saved, a measured result) that the brief supplies.
- **Not when:** the number is invented, tiny (a count of 3), or part of a table; or there are more than four on the screen. Never count up a number you cannot source.
- **Reduced motion:** `countUp` returns at once: the final number is the only number.
- **Recipe:** [number-counter.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/number-counter.md)

### Marquee

A single row of words, logos or tags drifts sideways in a loop.

- **Use when:** a strip of partner names the brief supplies, a ribbon of keywords, a kinetic divider between sections.
- **Not when:** the row carries information people must read (a marquee is unreadable by design), or when you would invent logos or clients.
- **Reduced motion:** The animation is only declared inside `no-preference`. In the reduced case the row wraps and the copy list is hidden: a still, complete list.
- **Recipe:** [marquee.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/marquee.md)

### Step scrollytelling

Text steps scroll past while one sticky graphic changes state to match the step in view. The reader sets the pace; each step changes one thing.

- **Use when:** explaining a process, a chart with several states, a data story, a before-and-after.
- **Not when:** there are no distinct states (use a scrubbed scene instead), or the text is the whole content and the graphic adds nothing.
- **Reduced motion:** States still change on scroll, in cuts (no transition). Nothing travels.
- **Recipe:** [step-scrollytelling.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/step-scrollytelling.md)

### Pinned scene, scrubbed by scroll

A tall section holds one scene on screen while scroll progress (0 to 1) drives it: a camera move, a reveal, a drawing, captions that arrive in order.

- **Use when:** one idea needs 200 to 300% of a screen to unfold; a 3D object changing pose; a diagram assembling.
- **Not when:** the content is a list of facts (use steps), the section would pin longer than about 300% of a screen, or the brief wants normal scrolling.
- **Reduced motion:** Nothing pins and nothing scrubs: the scene is a normal block in its finished state.
- **Recipe:** [pinned-scene-scrub.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/pinned-scene-scrub.md)

### Horizontal scroll section

Vertical scrolling pushes a row of panels sideways, then the page carries on down.

- **Use when:** a timeline, a gallery or a set of case studies that suits a left-to-right order, on a wide screen.
- **Not when:** on phones, with reduced motion, or when the content is something people compare or scan (a table, pricing). Never hijack the scroll direction without a way past it.
- **Reduced motion:** A native swipe row with scroll snap: the same content, no pin, no hijack, keyboard scrollable (`tabindex="0"` on the track if it has no focusable children).
- **Recipe:** [horizontal-scroll.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/horizontal-scroll.md)

### Image sequence scrubbed by scroll

A run of numbered pictures draws to a canvas, and scroll picks the frame: the "video that follows your scroll" effect, for a product turning, a flower opening, a render flying through.

- **Use when:** the brief has a rendered or filmed object whose motion the reader should control.
- **Not when:** the motion is simple enough to do with CSS, the frames would exceed the page weight budget, or the effect has no story.
- **Reduced motion:** The canvas shows the last frame and nothing scrubs. The page needs no pin.
- **Recipe:** [image-sequence-scrub.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/image-sequence-scrub.md)

### Parallax depth

Layers move at different speeds as the page scrolls, which gives a flat page a sense of depth.

- **Use when:** one hero or one divider, lightly, where the brief asks for "depth" or "layers".
- **Not when:** the whole page, text layers, or large travel. A 2013 study found parallax did not improve the experience, and it makes some people feel ill. Skip it if the brief is not specific.
- **Reduced motion:** No drift at all: the layers sit at their rest position (the CSS is only declared inside `no-preference`, the script returns).
- **Recipe:** [parallax-depth.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/parallax-depth.md)

### Scroll progress bar

A thin bar at the top of the page fills as the reader scrolls: a quiet cue for long articles and stories.

- **Use when:** a long read, an article, a scroll story where "how far" helps.
- **Not when:** a short page, or where the bar would sit over a fixed nav and add noise.
- **Reduced motion:** Kept, through the listener path above. If a stricter brief wants no bar at all, delete the listener branch and show nothing.
- **Recipe:** [scroll-progress-bar.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/scroll-progress-bar.md)

### 3D product that turns as you scroll

A real 3D object sits in a pinned scene and changes pose as the reader scrolls: turns, tilts, moves aside to make room for a caption.

- **Use when:** hardware, a physical product, an object whose shape is the selling point, with a model (`.glb`) from the user.
- **Not when:** there is no model and no time to make one (draw it in SVG or use an image sequence), or the page must run well on weak phones with no fallback.
- **Reduced motion:** One still frame; scroll changes the pose in cuts (each `invalidate` renders once), never a glide. The `still` flag from the stage drives this.
- **Recipe:** [product-3d-scroll.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/product-3d-scroll.md)

### Shader background

A full-screen fragment shader paints a slow, living background (noise, a gradient that drifts, contour lines) behind the content.

- **Use when:** a hero or a section that wants atmosphere the brief names: "flowing", "aurora", "liquid", "gradient mesh". One per page.
- **Not when:** text sits directly on it without a scrim, the page already has a 3D scene, or the brief wants calm and low power. Never as decoration on every section.
- **Reduced motion:** One frame at a fixed time (`stage.still`), no loop. A good still is part of the design: pick the time value with a screenshot.
- **Recipe:** [shader-background.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/shader-background.md)

### Magnetic button

A button leans a few pixels toward the pointer while the pointer is over it, then settles back when it leaves.

- **Use when:** one primary call to action on a pointer device, where the brief wants a tactile, playful feel.
- **Not when:** on touch screens, with reduced motion, on every link, or on small tap targets that would slip away from the finger. It must never make a control hard to hit.
- **Reduced motion:** Not created. The button is a plain button.
- **Recipe:** [magnetic-button.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/magnetic-button.md)

### Cursor follower

A soft dot or ring trails the pointer with a little lag, and grows over links.

- **Use when:** an expressive portfolio or an agency page, on desktop, where the brief asks for a custom cursor.
- **Not when:** on touch or with reduced motion; as a replacement for the real cursor (do not hide it: people lose track of the pointer); on pages for tasks or forms.
- **Reduced motion:** Not created: no dot is added, and the normal cursor is used with no lag and no growth.
- **Recipe:** [cursor-follower.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/cursor-follower.md)

### Tilt and spotlight cards

Cards tilt a few degrees toward the pointer and a soft light follows it across the surface.

- **Use when:** a row of feature or project cards on a pointer device, where the brief asks for "interactive", "premium" or "glow" cards.
- **Not when:** on touch, with reduced motion, for cards with small text that must stay still while read, or more than about six at once.
- **Reduced motion:** No listener is attached: flat cards, no light.
- **Recipe:** [tilt-spotlight-cards.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/tilt-spotlight-cards.md)

### Bento grid with motion

An asymmetric grid of cards of different sizes; the cards come in as a group, and each lifts slightly on hover.

- **Use when:** a features overview with five to nine items of unequal weight, a product summary, a dashboard-style section.
- **Not when:** the items are equal (use a plain grid), the content is a long list, or every card has a different animation.
- **Reduced motion:** `reveal` returns at once: all tiles visible. The hover lift is declared only inside `no-preference`.
- **Recipe:** [bento-motion.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/bento-motion.md)

### Page transition

Moving to another page of the site cross-fades with a small, matched slide instead of a hard flash.

- **Use when:** a multi-page site (portfolio, studio, documentation with a few pages) where the brief wants it to feel continuous.
- **Not when:** a single-page site, or when the brief needs a video or WebGL canvas to survive the navigation (the API cannot keep it alive; see `stacks/view-transitions.md` for routers).
- **Reduced motion:** The block is inside `no-preference`, so there is no transition and the page changes at once. `kit/kit.css` also switches off the view-transition pseudo-elements.
- **Recipe:** [page-transition.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/page-transition.md)

### Shared element morph

A card or thumbnail grows into the hero of its detail page, and shrinks back to its place on Back.

- **Use when:** a portfolio, case-study index, product grid or gallery with a detail page for each item.
- **Not when:** the two images have very different shapes (a square thumbnail into a wide banner stretches), many elements would morph at once, or the detail opens in a modal on the same page (use `layout-reorder` or a same-page transition).
- **Reduced motion:** Declared only inside `no-preference`: no morph, a plain page change. The kit's `sharedElementNav` adds names only when the API fires its events, which it does not without the opt-in.
- **Recipe:** [shared-element-morph.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/shared-element-morph.md)

### Layout change: filter, sort, reorder

When a grid is filtered or sorted, the cards glide to their new places instead of jumping.

- **Use when:** a filterable portfolio, a sortable list, a gallery with tags, a dashboard whose cards reorder.
- **Not when:** the order changes constantly (a live feed), or there are hundreds of items. Never animate the content a person is trying to read mid-change.
- **Reduced motion:** `transition()` runs the update directly: same result, no travel.
- **Recipe:** [layout-reorder.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/layout-reorder.md)

### Theme toggle transition

Switching between light and dark crossfades the whole page, or wipes from the button, instead of flashing.

- **Use when:** the brief asks for a dark or light switch, and the page supports both.
- **Not when:** the page has one theme, or the colour change would flash large areas for people sensitive to light (keep it a soft crossfade, never a strobe).
- **Reduced motion:** `set(next)` runs directly: an instant switch.
- **Recipe:** [theme-toggle-transition.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/theme-toggle-transition.md)

### Section colour shift

As the reader moves from chapter to chapter, the page background and text colours change to the chapter's own palette.

- **Use when:** a story or a launch page with distinct chapters that each deserve a mood.
- **Not when:** a utility page, long reading text (changing contrast while reading tires people), or more than about five chapters.
- **Reduced motion:** The transition is declared only inside `no-preference`, so the colours switch at once: this is a cut, which is allowed. If a brief asks for no change at all, drop the script and use one palette.
- **Recipe:** [section-colour-shift.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/section-colour-shift.md)

### Scroll-snap carousel

A row of cards swipes sideways and each one snaps into place; buttons move it for people with a mouse or keyboard.

- **Use when:** testimonials the user supplies, products, case studies, steps: anything with three to ten similar items in a row.
- **Not when:** the items need to be compared side by side, or the row hides the only call to action. Never auto-advance.
- **Reduced motion:** `scroll-behavior: smooth` is declared only in `no-preference`, and the buttons use `behavior: 'auto'`: jumps, not glides.
- **Recipe:** [scroll-snap-carousel.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/scroll-snap-carousel.md)

### SVG line drawing

A line, an outline or a chart curve draws itself from start to end, once or tied to scroll.

- **Use when:** a signature underline, a route or timeline, a hand-drawn diagram, a chart line. The line is the story.
- **Not when:** the shape is a filled icon, or many small lines draw at once (it reads as noise).
- **Reduced motion:** `prepareDraw` leaves the offset at 0: the whole line is there. `animateDraw` returns no animations.
- **Recipe:** [svg-line-draw.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/svg-line-draw.md)

### Lottie or Rive animation spot

A small designer-made animation (an icon, an illustration, an interactive mascot) plays where it is needed and nowhere else.

- **Use when:** the user supplies a Lottie JSON or a `.riv` file, or the brief names After Effects, Lottie or Rive.
- **Not when:** nothing is supplied and the motion is simple (draw it in SVG with the kit), the file is large, or the licence of the file is unknown.
- **Reduced motion:** Lottie loads paused on `stillFrame`; Rive draws one frame. Neither loops.
- **Recipe:** [lottie-rive-spot.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/lottie-rive-spot.md)

### Dust that forms a picture

Dots or dust drift in and assemble into a product, logo, face or word, then burst apart and re-form into the next shape as the page scrolls.

- **Use when:** the brief wants particles, dust, dots, halftone or stipple that become something.
- **Not when:** nothing needs to be formed (use a simple background), or a still image does the job. It is a heavy effect: one per page.
- **Reduced motion:** The finished state is shown still (the engine keeps a still image of the formed shape for this and for no WebGL); the page scrolls normally and nothing travels.
- **Recipe:** [particles-form.md](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/particles-form.md)

## Adding a pattern

Write the page in [skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/](../skills/brief2motion/references/patterns/) with the same sections as the others, add it to the index in its README and to `patterns` in `references/routing.json`, then run `node docs/build_motion_patterns.mjs` and `node --test tests/*.test.mjs`.
